title: Power of Two
summary: Determine if an integer is a power of two by checking if there exists an integer x such that the given number equals 2 raised to the power of x.
statement: Determine if an integer is a power of two by checking if there exists an integer x such that the given number equals 2 raised to the power of x.
constraints: The exponent is a nonnegative integer; 1 equals 2^0.
hints: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit.
Clearing the lowest set bit should leave zero, but positivity must be checked separately.
Zero is not a power of two even though its bit-clearing result is zero.
editorial: For a positive integer, n & (n-1) clears its lowest one bit. The result is zero exactly when that was the only one bit, which characterizes powers of two. The positivity condition excludes zero and negatives. The independent oracle compares against the complete finite set of powers allowed by the 32-bit input range.

tests.explanation: 1 equals 2 to the zeroth power, so it qualifies.
3 lies between consecutive powers 2 and 4 and is not a power of two.
